extract:
Blå Tåget was a Stockholm group and one of the most literate and idiosyncratic bands of the Swedish progg movement, the politically engaged, Swedish-language alternative scene that flourished from the late 1960s through the 1970s. The band emerged around 1969 and was most active in the first half of the 1970s. Its members later reconvened in the 1980s and again around the turn of the millennium, so the group's history stretches across several decades.

The band grew out of a circle of Stockholm writers, artists and musicians rather than from the conventional rock circuit. Its core included the poet and critic Leif Nylén, Tore Berger, Torkel Rasmusson, Mats G Bengtsson and Kjell Westling. They first recorded under the name Gunder Hägg, a joking reference to the celebrated Swedish runner, and released their debut on the independent label Silence Records. After objections to the use of the athlete's name, they renamed themselves Blå Tåget. From the start their approach mixed amateur enthusiasm, art-world irony and sharp political wit, and they drew as much on cabaret, jazz and Swedish song traditions as on rock.

Brustna hjärtans hotell, released in 1972, is the record most closely associated with the band. Its best-known song is Staten och kapitalet, a pointed critique of the state and capital alike, with lyrics by Nylén. Slowfox followed in 1974 and continued the group's blend of wry lyrical observation and loose, eclectic arrangements. A live document, Blå Tåget på Fågel blå, appeared in 1982 and captured the reunited band in a Stockholm setting. Later studio work came with Moderna Material in 1999 and I tidens rififi in 2004, showing the group's older members still writing in the same ironic, intellectually restless vein.

Blå Tåget belonged to the Silence-centred independent network that defined much of Swedish progg, alongside the festival culture and alternative distribution that sustained the movement outside the commercial industry. Within that scene they stood apart for their literary sensibility, which owed much to Nylén's background in poetry and criticism. Their politics were also less dogmatic and more skeptical than those of many of their peers.

The band's cultural footprint grew far beyond its original audience when the punk group Ebba Grön recorded Staten och kapitalet in the early 1980s. Their version turned the song into one of the most widely known Swedish rock anthems and introduced Blå Tåget's writing to a new generation. The song has since been sung and referenced so widely that it is often regarded as a standard of Swedish protest music.

Archival interest in the band has continued. Melodisk Rock (Live) and Progglådan Blå Tåget (Live från SvR Tonkraft, 1977), both issued in 2013, preserved concert performances from their heyday. Leif Nylén died in 2016. Blå Tåget is remembered as one of the progg era's most intelligent voices, a band whose ironic, questioning songs outlasted the movement that produced them.
title: Blå Tåget
